question: How do different powers draw in other powers during contemplation?
premises: Some powers are infinite, while others are limited.
A power can draw in other powers according to the rule of the qualities present in it.
This drawing in depends on nearness and distance.
inference: The scope and proximity of a contemplated power determine which other powers it can encompass.
uncertainties: The compound 'dhavatāsattvanyāyāt' is terse; the reading follows the sense of qualities being present and operative.
plain_english: There, some power may be infinite or limited, and it may draw in other powers according to the rule of the qualities present in it, depending on nearness and distance.
